title: Published Abaqus rate-independent Mises plasticity uniaxial state
purpose: Compare AgentFEM's global three-dimensional J2 procedure with the material data and homogeneous uniaxial state published in the Abaqus rate-independent plasticity verification manual.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain Mises plasticity with linear isotropic hardening

source.title: Rate-independent plasticity
source.case: Mises plasticity with isotropic hardening; homogeneous uniaxial C3D8 verification data

execution.evidence: For E=200000, nu=0.3 and the published hardening points (yield stress, plastic strain)=(200,0) and (220,0.0009), a homogeneous total axial strain of 0.002 must recover axial stress 220 and equivalent plastic strain 0.0009.

observables: Mean axial stress at total axial strain 0.002.
Mean equivalent plastic strain at the same converged state.
acceptance: Mean axial stress equals 220 within the versioned numerical tolerance.
Mean equivalent plastic strain equals 0.0009 within the versioned numerical tolerance.

quantities.name: mean_axial_stress
quantities.description: Second published isotropic-hardening point under homogeneous uniaxial deformation.

quantities.name: mean_equivalent_plastic_strain
quantities.description: Published equivalent plastic strain paired with yield stress 220.

limitations: This reproduces a published homogeneous constitutive verification state; it is not an experimental material validation.

AgentFEM uses its native tetrahedral unit-cube patch rather than the Abaqus C3D8 input file, so this contract isolates constitutive/global-equilibrium agreement rather than element-by-element equivalence.
Only the first linear hardening segment is represented by the current AgentFEM material law.
